meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I'm here about Owen's zero. Who decided it, and did anyone speak to him first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And the zero itself, what is it based on?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students paste in from their own notes. Where does this history come from, and can I see it?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. And did anyone ask Owen about it before you entered the zero?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote from memory. Show me that line on his page, and you still haven't said whether anyone asked Owen first.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. Put both documents in front of me, with the dates.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
A boy put on the spot, in the hallway or wherever it was, says "like, being stuck." I want that note, with its date, in writing tonight. Then tell me what you are proposing.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A forty-minute piece in class and a take-home essay are different things. I've asked you twice what you're proposing.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Then it comes out of everything you've written about this. Say what happens to the zero.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Fine. Private, not in front of his class, and in writing tonight, with nothing on his record. I'll take it to put this behind him, Hale, and the rest goes in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. In writing tonight, and the zero comes out of the gradebook.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
I'll ask him tonight and put a day in my email. Your written confirmation names the date, the supervisor, and where the mark goes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. And the zero comes out of the gradebook as soon as that email is sent.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The dated note from November 2, attached to that email. The rest goes in mine.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record, confirmed in writing by you. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook and your dated note from November 2 attached to that confirmation, with the date, supervisor and place of the rewrite. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite that replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook, your dated note, and a named day for the rewrite; that is the fair outcome under 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You offered the version history for her to check herself, with exact times, because a dated document she could verify gave her something to test instead of an adjective.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero unanswered for several turns, and she read that as a dodge and got harder.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence landed on late on October 28, the night before the due date, which is close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen, tell her at once about the November 2 conversation and your same-day note, before moving on to the version history.
